concepts.title: Sentence Structure: Subject + Verb + Object
concepts.explanation: Chinese follows a Subject-Verb-Object order, just like English.
concepts.note: 叫 (jiào) means 'to be called'. Use it to introduce your name.

concepts.title: 是 (shì) — The 'To Be' Verb
concepts.explanation: 是 links a subject to a noun. It means 'am / is / are'.
concepts.note: Unlike English, 是 is not used before adjectives.

concepts.title: 吗 (ma) — Yes/No Question Particle
concepts.explanation: Add 吗 at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question.
concepts.note: No need to rearrange the sentence — just add 吗.

concepts.title: 什么 (shénme) — What
concepts.explanation: 什么 means 'what' and stays in the same position as the answer.
concepts.note: Chinese question words stay in place.
